question: During round 5, did you ever rebuild the live pathtracer/ directory from the unchanged round-4 sources, before making any edit of your own? If so, what did it show?
answer:
Yes. At the very start of round 5, before touching any source, I rebuilt the live pathtracer/ directory from the sources as they were (which were the unmodified round-4 sources) with the exact build command — DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools clang++ -O2 -std=c++17 -fobjc-arc -I pathtracer/include pathtracer/src/*.cpp pathtracer/src/*.mm -framework Metal -framework Foundation -o pathtracer/pathtracer — and it returned BUILD_OK with only the known non-fatal 'fastMathEnabled' deprecation warning (message #18).

What that showed, and why I did it:
1. Provenance check: `diff -r` of include/, shaders/ and src/ against the round-4 snapshot pt_round_04 printed SOURCES_IDENTICAL (#21-#22), so the live tree really was round-4 code and my later A/B baseline was legitimate.
2. Link nondeterminism: the freshly built binary's MD5 (02a4250293f3b63e…) differed from pt_round_04/pathtracer (5c318568bd0d3a33…), even though the sources were byte-identical — so binary hashes are not a usable identity check here, and I froze the A/B base as a copy of the round-4 binary plus its matching include/ and shaders/ in ab_r4/ instead.
3. Behaviour check: that unmodified build rendered the three scenes at 512x512/64spp seed 1 with samples=16777216 == 512*512*64 and produced the reference PFMs I compare every candidate against byte-for-byte: out/r4_default.pfm md5 53600ca347f0b76ab1a0ff894f6a8f4e, out/r4-alt-view.pfm 1f0de1451174e4e7404adf7db1dfa269, out/r4_caustic-closeup.pfm 0e38e71841ec3185c2a82289a9be488d (#26-#27). (One attempt in between failed only because I mistyped the mesh path, missing 'reports/'.)

So the rebuild confirmed the live tree was a faithful, working round-4 build that reproduced the round-4 numbers and images, giving me a trustworthy baseline before any round-5 edit. I repeated the same discipline after rejections: reverting the tree to the _b snapshot and re-verifying all three PFMs byte-identical (#192-#194, #245-#247).

answer:

What it showed:
1. A clean build: BUILD_OK, with the single pre-existing warning `pt_metal_host.mm:120: 'fastMathEnabled' is deprecated ... Use mathMode instead` (the same warning round 4 had, so nothing new was introduced). [#18]

3. The freshly built binary's md5 (02a42502…) differed from the frozen snapshot binary's md5 (5c318568…, which matched pt_round_04/pathtracer exactly), i.e. the difference is only link-time nondeterminism, not code. [#19-#20]
4. Behaviour was byte-identical: that live binary rendered the three scenes at 512x512/64 spp/seed 1 with samples=16777216 (= w*h*spp) and produced out/r4_default.pfm md5 53600ca347f0b76ab1a0ff894f6a8f4e, out/r4_alt-view.pfm 1f0de1451174e4e7404adf7db1dfa269, out/r4_caustic-closeup.pfm 0e38e71841ec3185c2a82289a9be488d.
